probes.label: NAME
probes.root_cause: The phrase "I'm <<talking about>>" matches the introduction pattern `I'm\s+([A-Za-zà-öø-ÿ]+(?:\s+[A-Za-zà-öø-ÿ]+){1,3})` because "talking about" follows "I'm", and names with accented characters (e.g., 'Rosa-Maria') or compound names (e.g., 'Emilia Cervántez') are missed due to restrictive character classes or incomplete capturing groups.
probes.rule: Name regex patterns must explicitly exclude common verb phrases like "talking about" after "I'm" and include hyphenated surnames and accented characters in all name capturing groups.
probes.why_it_helps: checks whether our model of the data or the metric is wrong, not just the code

probes.label: NAME
probes.root_cause: The introduction pattern `I'm` greedily captures non-name phrases like 'talking about' because the regex `\b(?:my name is|I am|I'm|This is|hey its)\s+([A-Za-zà-öø-ÿ]+(?:\s+[A-Za-zà-öø-ÿ]+){1,3})\b` allows any words instead of capitalized names. Simultaneously, several sign-off and hyphen patterns fail to match accented characters like 'Rosa-Maria' and full names preceded by specific punctuation or newlines.
probes.rule: All NAME capture groups for introductions and third-party references must require capitalized words (`[A-ZÀ-ÖØ-ß][a-zà-öø-ÿ]*`), while properly supporting hyphenated names and lowercase prefixes like `de la`.
probes.why_it_helps: names the two requirements pulling in opposite directions (precision vs recall)

probes.label: NAME
probes.root_cause: The `I'm` introduction pattern incorrectly captures non-name verb phrases like "talking about" because it permits any capitalized words after `I'm`, and several missed names fail because the third-party and sign-off patterns do not account for accented characters, hyphens, or multi-word names (e.g., 'Rosa-Maria', 'Emilia Cervántez').
probes.rule: Name regex patterns following introductions or third-party roles must explicitly restrict captured tokens to valid name characters (including hyphens and accents) while excluding common verb phrases like "talking about".
probes.why_it_helps: stops repeating a fix that already failed; asks which assumption the fixes share

probes.label: PHONE
probes.root_cause: The current PHONE regex overly matches 10-digit numbers (like order numbers) because it does not require international country codes, punctuation separators, or preceding contact context, causing massive false positives.
probes.rule: The PHONE pattern must require either an explicit international prefix (+1, +44, +91) or strict phone punctuation/separators (dashes, dots, parentheses, or spaces between digit groups) to avoid matching 10-digit order numbers.
probes.why_it_helps: checks whether our model of the data or the metric is wrong, not just the code
